_note: Illustrative figures compiled for a portfolio project. Rates and fees change often and vary by lender — always verify with the lender or the official scheme portal before acting.

docs.overview: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) Shishu category offers collateral-free micro loans up to Rs 50,000 to non-farm micro enterprises in manufacturing, trading and services. Loans are given through banks, NBFCs and MFIs and are covered by the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU), so no collateral or third-party guarantee is needed.
docs.eligibility: Any Indian citizen with a business plan for a non-farm income generating activity in manufacturing, processing, trading or services. Suitable for new and very small businesses. No minimum business vintage. Borrower should not be a defaulter to any bank.
docs.fees: Processing fee is generally waived for Shishu loans. No collateral. No guarantee fee is charged to the borrower. Interest typically 9 to 12 percent per annum depending on the lender. Repayment up to 5 years.

docs.overview: Mudra Kishore loans cover Rs 50,001 to Rs 5 lakh for micro enterprises that want to buy equipment, stock or expand an existing small business. Collateral-free and backed by CGFMU.
docs.eligibility: Non-farm micro enterprises in manufacturing, trading or services. New units are allowed but lenders usually expect a basic project report. Typical lender expectation of a credit score of 650 or above and around 10 percent promoter margin.
docs.fees: Processing fee around 0.5 percent of the loan, many banks cap it near Rs 2,500, plus 18 percent GST on the fee. No collateral and no guarantee fee to borrower. Interest typically 10 to 13.5 percent. Tenure up to 7 years with up to 6 months moratorium.

docs.overview: Mudra Tarun loans cover Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for growing micro enterprises. Collateral-free under CGFMU. (A Tarun Plus category up to Rs 20 lakh exists for borrowers who have repaid an earlier Tarun loan; it is not modelled here.)
docs.eligibility: Micro enterprises with a viable project report. Lenders typically expect a credit score of about 680 or more, promoter contribution of at least 10 percent, and finance up to 90 percent of project cost.
docs.fees: Processing fee about 0.5 percent of loan amount capped near Rs 5,000 plus GST. No collateral, no guarantee fee charged to borrower. Interest about 10.5 to 14 percent. Tenure up to 7 years.

docs.overview: Stand-Up India gives bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch, for setting up a greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services or trading. The loan is composite (term loan plus working capital) and can cover up to 75 percent of project cost.
docs.eligibility: Woman entrepreneurs or SC/ST entrepreneurs above 18 years. Only greenfield (first-time) ventures qualify. For non-individual enterprises at least 51 percent shareholding must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur. Borrower should not be in default. Borrower contribution of at least 10 percent of project cost.
docs.fees: Interest is the bank's lowest applicable rate for the category, typically base rate (MCLR) plus 3 percent plus tenor premium, around 9.5 to 11.5 percent. Processing fee about 0.5 percent. Security is primary assets plus collateral, or a guarantee cover under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India (CGSSI) / CGTMSE. Repayment up to 7 years with up to 18 months moratorium.

docs.overview: PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy programme run by KVIC for new micro enterprises. Maximum project cost is Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs 20 lakh for service units. Trading activities are not eligible. The government margin money subsidy reduces the effective debt.
docs.eligibility: Individuals above 18 years setting up a new (greenfield) unit; existing units and units that already availed a government subsidy are not eligible. Own contribution is 10 percent of project cost for general category and 5 percent for special category (SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women/ex-servicemen/PwD/NER/hill and border areas).
docs.fees: Margin money subsidy: general category 15 percent of project cost in urban areas and 25 percent in rural areas; special category 25 percent urban and 35 percent rural. Subsidy is kept as a term deposit for 3 years and adjusted against the loan. No collateral for loans up to Rs 10 lakh, and loans are covered by CGTMSE. Normal bank interest rates apply, around 10 to 12 percent. Repayment 3 to 7 years after an initial moratorium.

docs.overview: Secured term loans from public and private sector banks for purchase of machinery, plant expansion or capex by established MSMEs. Funding up to about 80 percent of project cost.
docs.eligibility: Usually requires at least 2 years of business vintage with filed ITRs and GST returns, a credit score of about 700 or more, and 20 to 25 percent promoter margin. Collateral (property or fixed deposits) or a CGTMSE guarantee is required.
docs.fees: Processing fee 0.5 to 1 percent of the sanctioned amount plus 18 percent GST. Interest linked to the bank's EBLR or MCLR, roughly 9.25 to 12.5 percent. Foreclosure charges up to 2 percent on fixed-rate loans. Tenure up to 10 years.

docs.overview: The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) guarantees collateral-free loans given by member lending institutions to micro and small enterprises, up to Rs 5 crore per borrower. It is not a loan itself; it replaces the collateral requirement on a bank loan.
docs.eligibility: New and existing micro and small enterprises in manufacturing, services and retail trade, borrowing from a member bank or NBFC. The loan must be free of collateral and third-party guarantee.
docs.fees: Annual guarantee fee is charged on the outstanding amount. Illustrative slabs: 0.37 percent up to Rs 10 lakh, 0.55 percent from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh, 0.60 percent from Rs 50 lakh to Rs 1 crore, and about 1.2 percent above Rs 1 crore. Concessions apply for women, SC/ST and some regions. The fee is usually passed on to the borrower.

docs.overview: Unsecured business loans from NBFCs and digital lenders. Fast disbursal (2 to 7 days) with minimal paperwork, but considerably more expensive than bank or government scheme credit.
docs.eligibility: Business vintage of at least 1 year, credit score of about 680 or more, regular bank statements and GST filings. Loan size is usually linked to turnover.
docs.fees: Interest 16 to 24 percent per annum. Processing fee up to 2 percent plus GST. Foreclosure charges 2 to 4 percent. Tenure up to 4 years. No collateral.

schemes.name: Bank Cash Credit / Working Capital Limit

docs.overview: Cash credit and overdraft limits fund day-to-day working capital such as inventory and receivables. Interest is charged only on the amount actually drawn. Limits are renewed every year.
docs.eligibility: Businesses with at least 1 year of operations and stock/receivables to hypothecate. Drawing power is computed on current assets after a margin of about 25 percent. Collateral or CGTMSE cover needed.
docs.fees: Interest about 9.5 to 12 percent on utilised amount. Processing and annual renewal fee about 0.5 percent of the limit plus GST. Limit tenure 12 months, renewable.

docs.overview: Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platforms such as RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart let MSMEs sell invoices raised on large corporates, PSUs and government departments to financiers through an auction, getting cash before the buyer pays.
docs.eligibility: MSMEs registered on Udyam that sell to buyers registered on TReDS (large corporates, PSUs, government). No collateral. Pricing depends on the buyer's credit rating, not the MSME's.
docs.fees: Discount rate typically 7.5 to 11 percent annualised, linked to buyer rating. Small one-time onboarding and annual platform fees. Without recourse to the MSME. Only funds receivables, so it suits working capital needs, not capex.
